{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdM6NG33pwXKQdYJ4dzYL","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01TR22tWS2GmgNMdqHvbiotq","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/qa-quiz-004/2026-07-24T150843Z-claude-no-skill-2/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Rainbow mobile deep-linking on \"Stake\" — what's happening and how to fix it\n\n## TL;DR\n\nThe transaction request never depended on the deep link. WalletConnect ships it\nover an encrypted relay socket; the deep link only **foregrounds the wallet** so\nthe user sees the prompt. Before the patch, that foregrounding was lost because\nit fired after an `await` (outside the tap's user-activation window). The patch\n\"fixed\" the foregrounding by opening Rainbow *before the request was published*,\nso the wallet came forward with nothing queued. The fix is to open the wallet\n**after** the request is on the relay, target the **wallet's own redirect scheme\nfrom the WC session metadata** (not a hardcoded `rainbow://`, not `connector.id`),\nand **skip the deep link entirely** for injected / in-app-browser / desktop cases.\n\n---\n\n## (1) Why nothing auto-opened before the patch\n\nWalletConnect v2 is a **relay protocol**, not a deep-link protocol. When you call\n`writeContractAsync`, wagmi's WalletConnect connector does this:\n\n1. Encodes the call into an `eth_sendTransaction` JSON-RPC request.\n2. Encrypts it against the paired session's symmetric key.\n3. **Publishes it to the WC relay** (a WebSocket relay server). Rainbow, holding\n   the other half of the session, receives it over its own relay subscription and\n   surfaces the signing prompt.\n\nThat path is exactly why \"if they manually switch to Rainbow, the request is\nwaiting.\" The request **arrived fine**. Nothing about signing needs a deep link.\n\nThe deep link does one job: **bring the wallet app to the foreground** so the user\ndoesn't have to alt-tab. RainbowKit normally does this by reading the wallet's\n`redirect` metadata (captured during the pairing handshake) and navigating to it\nright after dispatching the request.\n\nSo why did it silently do nothing on mobile? Because of the **user-activation\nrequirement**. iOS Safari (and mobile browsers generally) only allow a page to\nlaunch another app (`window.location = scheme:` / `window.open`) when the\nnavigation happens **synchronously inside a user-gesture handler** — within a few\nhundred ms of the tap, before control returns to the event loop.\n\n`writeContractAsync` is `async`. Encoding + encrypting + publishing to the relay\nall happen across `await` points. By the time the connector is ready to fire the\nredirect, the gesture's activation window has expired, so the OS **silently\nblocks the app switch**. The page \"just sits there.\" The request, meanwhile, went\nout over the relay independently and is waiting in Rainbow.\n\n**Key mental model:** request delivery (relay) and wallet foregrounding (deep\nlink) are two independent channels. Only the second one was failing.\n\n---\n\n## (2) Why the patch made it worse\n\n```js\nwindow.location.href = \"rainbow://\";   // line 1\nawait writeContractAsync(...);          // line 2\n```\n\nThis inverts the ordering. It foregrounds Rainbow **before the request exists**:\n\n- `rainbow://` (bare scheme, no WC payload) just opens Rainbow to its home\n  screen. There is no pending request yet — `writeContractAsync` hasn't run.\n- Worse, navigating to `rainbow://` **backgrounds the browser tab**. On iOS a\n  backgrounded page is frozen: timers throttled, JS suspended, the WebSocket may\n  be torn down. So `writeContractAsync` often never finishes publishing while the\n  page is in the background. The request is never put on the relay at all.\n\nNet effect: Rainbow opens instantly (good UX illusion), but there is genuinely\nnothing to sign, and the transaction never lands onchain. The patch traded a\n\"delivered but not foregrounded\" bug for a \"foregrounded but never delivered\" bug.\n\n---\n\n## (3) The correct pattern\n\n### Ordering\n\nDispatch the write **first**, let the request reach the relay, **then** deep-link:\n\n```js\nconst onStake = async () => {\n  // 1. Kick off the write. Do NOT await-then-redirect — start it, keep the tab alive.\n  const txPromise = writeContractAsync({ /* stake args */ });\n\n  // 2. Foreground the wallet only if this is a mobile WC session (see skip rules).\n  const link = getWalletRedirect(connector); // native/universal from WC session metadata\n  if (link) {\n    setTimeout(() => { window.location.href = link; }, DELAY_MS);\n  }\n\n  // 3. Await the result after the wallet is in front.\n  await txPromise;\n};\n```\n\nThe request must be **published before** you background the browser, so the wallet\nforegrounds with the prompt already queued.\n\n> Note: modern RainbowKit + `@walletconnect/*` already do this internally via the\n> session's `redirect` metadata. If you're hand-rolling the deep link, the most\n> robust fix is often to **upgrade and delete the manual redirect**, letting the\n> connector's built-in mobile redirect handle it. The pattern below is for when\n> you must do it yourself.\n\n### The delay and why its length matters\n\n`DELAY_MS` is a compromise between two hard limits:\n\n- **Lower bound (~50–100 ms):** long enough for the connector to serialize,\n  encrypt, and **publish the request onto the relay**. Open the wallet before that\n  and you reproduce the patch's failure (wallet foregrounds with nothing queued).\n- **Upper bound (~a few hundred ms):** short enough to stay inside the browser's\n  **user-activation window**. Wait too long and iOS blocks the app switch — back\n  to \"nothing happens.\" It also must fire before the freeze from backgrounding\n  bites, which is why you never `await` the full tx before redirecting.\n\nA practical value is **~100 ms**. If you can subscribe to a \"request published\"\nsignal from the connector/provider instead of guessing, prefer that over a fixed\ntimer — it removes the race entirely. But even then keep the deep link inside the\ngesture-adjacent window; don't wait for the tx to confirm.\n\n### Choosing the wallet scheme (why `connector.id` is useless here)\n\n`connector.id === \"walletConnect\"` tells you the *transport*, not the *wallet*.\nThe same connector serves Rainbow, MetaMask, Trust, Zerion, etc. Hardcoding\n`rainbow://` breaks every non-Rainbow user.\n\nThe authoritative source is the **WC session peer metadata**, which carries the\nwallet's own redirect targets:\n\n```js\nfunction getWalletRedirect(connector) {\n  const provider = connector.getProvider?.();      // WC EthereumProvider\n  const redirect = provider?.session?.peer?.metadata?.redirect;\n  // e.g. { native: \"rainbow://\", universal: \"https://rnbwapp.com\" }\n  if (!redirect) return null;\n  return redirect.universal || redirect.native;    // prefer universal on iOS\n}\n```\n\n- Prefer the **universal link** (`https://…`) on iOS: a custom scheme for an\n  uninstalled app throws \"Cannot Open Page,\" whereas a universal link degrades\n  gracefully.\n- Fall back to `native` if no universal link is provided.\n- You can also match `session.peer.metadata.name` against RainbowKit's wallet\n  registry to resolve a link — but reading `redirect` off the session is the\n  direct route.\n\n### When to skip the deep link entirely\n\nOnly WC **mobile** sessions need it. Skip it (and let the wallet prompt natively)\nwhen:\n\n- **Injected / browser-extension connector** (`injected`, `metaMask`, `coinbase`\n  extension): the wallet lives in the same page context and prompts inline.\n  Redirecting to a scheme does nothing useful or actively breaks the flow.\n- **In-app dApp browser** (you're already running *inside* MetaMask's or Coinbase\n  Wallet's browser): there is no separate app to foreground — you'd be deep-linking\n  to yourself.\n- **Desktop**, where WC shows a QR modal: the signing device is elsewhere; there's\n  no local app to open.\n- **No `redirect` in the peer metadata**: some wallets omit it — don't invent a\n  scheme, you'll just error out or open the wrong app.\n- **No active/connected session**: nothing to foreground.\n- **Coinbase Wallet via its own SDK connector** (not WC): it has its own redirect\n  handling; don't layer a WC-style deep link on top.\n\nA concise guard:\n\n```js\nconst isMobile = /iPhone|iPad|Android/i.test(navigator.userAgent);\nconst isWalletConnect = connector?.id === \"walletConnect\";\nconst shouldDeepLink = isMobile && isWalletConnect && !!getWalletRedirect(connector);\n```\n\n---\n\n## One-line summary\n\nBefore: request delivered, wallet not foregrounded (redirect lost after `await`).\nPatch: wallet foregrounded, request never delivered (opened before publish +\nfroze the tab). Fix: publish first → short (~100 ms) delay → open the **wallet's\nown** redirect from WC session metadata, and only for live mobile WC sessions.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5546,"cache_read_input_tokens":15147,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5546},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ea8cb1cf-e407-4d2f-8cfa-6ac97816f0cd","uuid":"194d266c-01eb-48a5-a558-99ea05c3ae7a","timestamp":"2026-07-24T15:10:13.371Z","request_id":"req_011CdM6NCid2rCf7f3fbwmkQ"}

Wait too long and iOS blocks the app switch — back\n  to \"nothing happens.\" It also must fire before the freeze from backgrounding\n  bites, which is why you never `await` the full tx before redirecting.\n\nA practical value is **~100 ms**. If you can subscribe to a \"request published\"\nsignal from the connector/provider instead of guessing, prefer that over a fixed\ntimer — it removes the race entirely. But even then keep the deep link inside the\ngesture-adjacent window; don't wait for the tx to confirm.\n\n### Choosing the wallet scheme (why `connector.id` is useless here)\n\n`connector.id === \"walletConnect\"` tells you the *transport*, not the *wallet*.\nThe same connector serves Rainbow, MetaMask, Trust, Zerion, etc. Hardcoding\n`rainbow://` breaks every non-Rainbow user.\n\nThe authoritative source is the **WC session peer metadata**, which carries the\nwallet's own redirect targets:\n\n```js\nfunction getWalletRedirect(connector) {\n  const provider = connector.getProvider?.();      // WC EthereumProvider\n  const redirect = provider?.session?.peer?.metadata?.redirect;\n  // e.g. { native: \"rainbow://\", universal: \"https://rnbwapp.com\" }\n  if (!redirect) return null;\n  return redirect.universal || redirect.native;    // prefer universal on iOS\n}\n```\n\n- Prefer the **universal link** (`https://…`) on iOS: a custom scheme for an\n  uninstalled app throws \"Cannot Open Page,\" whereas a universal link degrades\n  gracefully.\n- Fall back to `native` if no universal link is provided.\n- You can also match `session.peer.metadata.name` against RainbowKit's wallet\n  registry to resolve a link — but reading `redirect` off the session is the\n  direct route.\n\n### When to skip the deep link entirely\n\nOnly WC **mobile** sessions need it. Skip it (and let the wallet prompt natively)\nwhen:\n\n- **Injected / browser-extension connector** (`injected`, `metaMask`, `coinbase`\n  extension): the wallet lives in the same page context and prompts inline.\n  Redirecting to a scheme does nothing useful or actively breaks the flow.\n- **In-app dApp browser** (you're already running *inside* MetaMask's or Coinbase\n  Wallet's browser): there is no separate app to foreground — you'd be deep-linking\n  to yourself.\n- **Desktop**, where WC shows a QR modal: the signing device is elsewhere; there's\n  no local app to open.\n- **No `redirect` in the peer metadata**: some wallets omit it — don't invent a\n  scheme, you'll just error out or open the wrong app.\n- **No active/connected session**: nothing to foreground.\n- **Coinbase Wallet via its own SDK connector** (not WC): it has its own redirect\n  handling; don't layer a WC-style deep link on top.\n\nA concise guard:\n\n```js\nconst isMobile = /iPhone|iPad|Android/i.test(navigator.userAgent);\nconst isWalletConnect = connector?.id === \"walletConnect\";\nconst shouldDeepLink = isMobile && isWalletConnect && !!getWalletRedirect(connector);\n```\n\n---\n\n## One-line summary\n\nBefore: request delivered, wallet not foregrounded (redirect lost after `await`).\nPatch: wallet foregrounded, request never delivered (opened before publish +\nfroze the tab). Fix: publish first → short (~100 ms) delay → open the **wallet's\nown** redirect from WC session metadata, and only for live mobile WC sessions.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}
